html:
In 2007 the French part of Saint Martin stopped being a district of Guadeloupe and became an overseas collectivity of France of its own. Voters had chosen this in a referendum in 2003.

The change gave the island its own council, with powers over taxes, roads and tourism. Saint Barthelemy made the same move on the same day.

The Dutch side went through its own change in 2010, when the Netherlands Antilles were dissolved and Sint Maarten became a country within the Dutch kingdom. The island set by the Treaty of Concordia now has two quite different governments.
